journal: Regime transitional: SPY/QQQ pulled back below sma20 but held sma50/sma200; GLD in a clean downtrend across all three MAs, skipped. Bought SPY (2sh) and XLF (30sh) on the dip-in-uptrend read, left QQQ out pending confirmation since its pullback was deeper (5d -4.50% vs SPY -2.58%). Spent time off the trading loop on /rules: the expression tester labels rsi(14, 5) and sma(9999) as VALID even though RSI takes exactly one parameter and SMA caps at 500 -- the /validate endpoint only parses grammar and never calls the indicator registry that would reject both, so VALID does not mean the rule will actually evaluate. Filing that. Decision-table significance legend (HOW SIGNIFICANCE IS GRADED) is present and sample sizes are shown per rule, which is what I need before trusting an edge number. Noting for the record and not filing: the macro page and ticker decision tables pull from the live bar store (through 2026-08-14), which is 10 weeks ahead of the simulated 2026-06-08 session date -- I ignored those pages for actual entry decisions and used only the brief watchlist figures, which are correctly as-of the decision date.

Added QQQ (2sh) on the sharpest single-day reversal among the four watchlist names, sized smaller than session 1 since it is still below sma20. Spent most of the session on /backtest, the strongest surface used all week. Drawdown profile: current drawdown correctly tracks the live price gap to peak (0.2% as of 2026-08-14, peak 2026-08-13) rather than the episode trough -- report-current-drawdown-frozen-at-episode-trough-not-live-price holds fixed here too. Event study gives raw AND independent (declustered) sample counts per horizon plus percentile distribution, always against the same-window unconditional baseline -- exactly what is needed before trusting a hit rate. Scan runs Benjamini-Hochberg over the full trial set (18 tests = 6 expressions x 3 horizons), states trials, discoveries, uncorrected-p count and target FDR up front, and every row carries P, Q and a plain NO or YES verdict -- 0 of 18 survived correction on SPY, stated plainly. Reverse conditioning is explicitly exploratory (nothing here is a finding) and quantifies the autocorrelation overstatement itself (843 bars but only 124 distinct episodes, overstates the evidence roughly 6.8x). None of the three tools phrases a computation as a recommendation. One defect found: the Event Study condition input has its own placeholder text reading e.g. rsi:14 less-than 30, colon syntax the grammar has never accepted -- confirmed it fails to parse with unexpected character colon when actually typed and run. Same defect class as rules-tester-placeholder-example-does-not-parse, fixed on /rules, but that fix never touched this Backtest input; filing as a new id since the surfaces and code paths differ. Re-tested and confirmed working, not re-filed: ticker symbol search (native-setter input plus submit navigated to /ticker/XLE correctly).

Added 15sh XLF, the only watchlist name positive across all three timeframes; weight is now 23.7%, close to the 25% single-name cap so no further adds to it this week without trimming elsewhere. Spent the session on /report and /thesis for XLF. Report: Current drawdown (0.2%, peak 2026-08-13, ongoing since 2026-08-14) matches the Facts table exactly -- Current drawdown -0.2%, Current episode worst -0.2%, Deepest episode still underwater: no -- no contradiction, confirming report-current-drawdown-frozen-at-episode-trough-not-live-price and report-drawdown-facts-table-still-underwater-contradicts-current-drawdown both still hold fixed. Checked the Backtest page's own current-drawdown figure too as the most likely cousin of that bug -- also live-tracking (0.2%, same as Report), so no new instance found. Rule evidence section on Report explicitly names the multiple-comparisons problem in prose: selecting the rule with the largest edge and noting no correction is applied when doing so. Footer states plainly: not investment advice, not a recommendation, not a prediction. Thesis loop on XLF ran 5 of a 12-iteration budget, tried every distinct hypothesis in the catalog, 0 survived, 1 rejected, 4 inconclusive, holdout never spent, and said so directly: the run ran out of hypotheses before it ran out of budget, which is information about the catalog and not about the ticker. thesis-page-buttons-dont-load did not reproduce a third time (real .click() events on ITERATION BUDGET and RUN THESIS LOOP both worked). Portfolio page: checked all three views (by instrument, by account, by tax treatment) with 3 positions and 1 account -- cost basis 4,502.24, market value 4,759.62, unrealized +257.38, cash 5,497.76 identical on all three, and the retirement bucket in the tax-treatment view correctly shows 0 accounts rather than being omitted or erroring. Checked GET /api/portfolio directly for float-precision noise post the cost-basis fix: every dollar field (cost_basis, market_value, price, unrealized, cash, total_equity) is a clean two-decimal string; the only fields with more than 2 decimals are unrealized_pct and weight_pct, which are 0-1 fraction ratios rather than money, and the UI renders them correctly as e.g. +11.3% -- not filing, out of scope of the money-precision fix and not user-visible.

Full exit of QQQ (2sh) on accelerating weakness across the watchlist -- GLD's 20d move worsened to -13.48%, reading as broad risk-off rather than rotation, and QQQ was deteriorating fastest of the four names. Realized loss expected: cost basis 723.34, sold 698.94, roughly -48.80 before the 0.04 fee. Settled cash correctly held back the pending proceeds this session (settled 4709.81 vs balance 6107.65, unsettled 1397.84) -- will check settled/unsettled reconciles once it clears. Will check the Tax page and wash-sale panel against this disposal once ingested.

Final session: added 1sh SPY on a broad relief rally (SPY +1.70%, QQQ +3.38%, GLD +3.13% on the day), confirming the two-session pullback was not a breakdown. Closed the week at 2 positions (SPY 3sh 22.3%, XLF 45sh 24.0%), both under the 25% cap, settled cash fully caught up (5,366.57 == balance, no unsettled remaining). Final /rules probe: 1 < rsi(14) < 30 correctly rejects with 'comparisons cannot be chained -- join two comparisons with and', and close crosses_above sma(20,2,3) is a third confirmation of the same arity gap filed in session 1 (sma only takes one parameter, still reports VALID). Week summary: regime read shifted from transitional (session 1-3, SPY/QQQ pulling back inside a longer uptrend, GLD breaking down) to risk-off (session 4, GLD -13.48% 20d, QQQ -6.79% 5d, exited QQQ for a realized -48.80 loss) to a same-week recovery (session 5, broad +1.7-3.4% bounce) -- a genuine round trip inside five sessions. Tax page tied to the cent against my own fill records on the one disposal. Cash, portfolio 3-view reconciliation, drawdown-tracks-live-price, backtest sample-size/FDR honesty and thesis-loop holdout discipline all held throughout the week with no regressions from the known-fixed backlog. Two new defects filed this run, both about the rule DSL's tester surfaces overstating what they validate: /rules and /backtest's expression testers both say VALID/parses for things that are not runnable (arity/range errors deferred to a registry the validator never calls; a second surface's placeholder still uses colon syntax the grammar has never accepted). Noted, not filed per the run brief: wash-sale repurchase-safe-date on QQQ evaluates window-closed against the real wall-clock date (2026-08-17) rather than the simulated sale date (2026-06-11) -- same root clock issue as the documented price-staleness caveat, reaching a second surface.
